pride_data.title: Mapping the lipid droplet proteome by using proximity labeling in ccRCC cell lines
pride_data.projectDescription: Comprehensive understanding of the lipid droplet (LD) proteome in ccRCC cells is lacking. In this study, we employed TurboID, an engineered biotin ligase with great efficiency for enzyme-catalyzed proximity labeling, to map the spatial proteome of LDs in ccRCC cells.
pride_data.sampleProcessingProtocol: To address proximity labeling of LD membrane, we generated ccRCC cell lines which stably expressing V5-tagged TurboID fused to the C terminal of LD marker protein HILPDA, and the cytoplasmic contrast TurboID fused with NES (nuclear export signal, NES). Next, to map the proteome of LDs, liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry was used to determine identify and quantify proteins isolated by affinity purification from HILPDA and NES cells with adequate biological and technical replicates
pride_data.dataProcessingProtocol: The protein identification and quantification was conducted in MaxQuant using lable free mode. Then R was used to do statistic analysis for identify potential LD related proteins.
